prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help. To point you to the best lawyer for your Pleasanton car-injury case I need a little more about your situation, but here are immediate steps, what to look for in an attorney, questions to ask, and next actions you can take right now.

Quick immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care and follow up — your health and medical records are critical to your case.
- Call 911 / file a police report if not already done.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries, witness contact info, repair estimates, and medical bills/records.
- Notify your insurer per policy requirements (give facts, don’t admit fault).
- Don’t sign releases, give recorded statements, or accept the insurer’s first settlement without talking to an attorney.

Important legal deadlines (California)
- Personal injury statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the date of injury. For claims against a government entity the deadline is much shorter (often 6 months) — act fast if that applies.
- There are other deadlines for filing insurance claims and for medical liens — don’t wait.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for:
- Specific experience with car-accident / personal injury cases (not just general practice).
- Trial experience and a record of either successful verdicts or good settlements.
- Experience handling similar injury severity (minor soft tissue vs. catastrophic injuries).
- Works on contingency fees (you typically pay only if they recover money).
- Clear communication style and a process for regular updates.
- Good client reviews and professional standing (no disciplinary history).

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident injury cases? How many similar cases have you taken to trial?
- Who will actually handle my file (attorney or staff)? Will I have direct contact with the attorney?
- What is your win/settlement track record for cases like mine?
- How do you charge? What percentage is your contingency fee? Are there any other costs I may be responsible for?
- How do you handle medical liens and unpaid medical providers?
- What is your estimate of the likely value/range of my case and timeline?
- Do you have references from past clients?
- Will I need to go to court? If so, how often have you tried similar cases?

What to bring to the consultation
- Police report number and a copy if available
- Photos of the accident scene, vehicles, and injuries
- Medical records and bills (or contact info for your treating providers)
- Insurance information for you and other drivers
- Any correspondence with insurers
- Names/contact of witnesses

Fee expectations and settlement timeline
- Contingency fees commonly range from about 33% (if settled before lawsuit) to 40% (if litigated/appealed) — get this spelled out in writing.
- Cases can settle in a few months (minor injuries) to 1–2+ years (serious injuries or disputed fault).

Where to find Pleasanton-area attorneys
- Use the California State Bar’s Lawyer Search to confirm license and discipline history.
- Get referrals from local sources: Alameda County Bar Association referral service, Yelp/Google reviews, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell.
- Interview at least 2–3 lawyers to compare.

I can do one of these next steps for you
- Find and list 3–5 Pleasanton or East Bay personal injury attorneys (with contact info and recent review summaries).
- Draft an email/phone script you can use to set up consultations.
- Help you evaluate responses you get from firms.

Tell me which of the above you want me to do, and give any brief details you’re comfortable sharing (date of accident, severity of injuries, whether police/insurer involved).
